SEON Partners with Yuno to Expand Global Fraud Prevention and Identity Verification
summary:
SEON, the AI Command Center for Fraud Prevention and AML Compliance, today announced a global partnership with Yuno, the AI-native intelligence system of global payments and financial services, powering the financial infrastructure of enterprise merchants, banks and wallets.
The partnership gives Yuno customers direct access to SEON’s fraud prevention and identity verification capabilities through the same infrastructure they use to manage payments globally. Yuno connects businesses to more than 1,000 payment methods across 190 countries through a single integration, while its vendor-agnostic model allows customers to choose the fraud and risk providers that best fit their needs.
Global payments infrastructure can scale quickly through orchestration, but fraud prevention often remains fragmented across markets and providers. For merchants expanding internationally, that creates gaps as fraud patterns change by geography, payment method and customer behavior. SEON’s platform evaluates risk throughout the full customer journey using 1,100+ real-time data signals spanning digital footprint, device intelligence and behavioral data across ongoing account activity.
“Merchants scaling internationally face fraud patterns that vary by market, payment method and customer behavior,” said Troy Nyi Nyi, SVP and GM, APAC, SEON. “Partnering with Yuno gives the businesses on their platform access to fraud prevention and identity verification that works across all of those dimensions without building a separate integration.”
“As businesses expand globally and want to improve their capabilities, their fraud and risk infrastructure needs to scale just as quickly as their payments infrastructure,” said Mauricio Schwartzmann, Chief Financial Services Officer, Yuno. “Our partnership with SEON gives customers a powerful option for managing fraud and identity verification across markets, all this enabled quickly through the same infrastructure they already use to manage their payments.”

content: SEON has announced a global partnership with Yuno to integrate its fraud prevention and identity verification capabilities into Yuno's payment infrastructure. PayJoy to Acquire Strategic Assets of Finia AI, Advancing AI Underwriting and Financial Product Innovation
summary:
PayJoy, a leading financial services provider for underserved consumers across emerging markets, today announced the acquisition of select strategic assets of Finia AI, Inc., a fintech company that developed AI-powered underwriting and financial products for micro-businesses in Mexico.
The transaction will enable PayJoy to apply Finia's technology and expertise to its global platform, strengthening its underwriting capabilities and expanding its financial product offering for customers with limited access to formal credit.
PayJoy has reached more than 20 million customers across nine countries in Latin America, Africa, and Asia through innovative financial products including digitally secured smartphone financing, credit lines, and the PayJoy Card. This acquisition brings technology developed specifically for the needs of small and informal businesses to a platform with the scale and reach to extend those innovations across global markets.
Finia built its AI underwriting capabilities to serve micro-businesses with limited financial data and owners with little or no formal credit history. The venture-backed fintech developed new ways to assess creditworthiness and applied them to offer financial products including credit cards and installment loans.
"I'm excited about the path ahead with PayJoy," said Uri Pomerantz, founder and CEO of Finia AI. "We've spent years building AI underwriting and financial products to serve micro-businesses in Latin America that traditional lenders too often overlook. PayJoy's global reach creates an opportunity to scale our technology and everything we've learned alongside one of the strongest teams in fintech. We share a commitment to improving customers' financial well-being, and this transaction opens a new chapter in that work."
"Finia has developed valuable technology and deep insights that can help address one of the fundamental challenges in financial inclusion: how to assess creditworthiness when traditional financial data is limited," said Jose Luis Gonzalez, Head of Growth for PayJoy Mexico. "Bringing these capabilities to PayJoy will strengthen our platform, enhance how we assess risk, and broaden our product offerings. We see a meaningful opportunity to extend the impact of Finia's work across the markets we serve."

DBS Group Research: The Next AI Race Moves Beyond Intelligence to Outcomes
summary:
Artificial intelligence is becoming more capable, more accessible and more widely deployed. In a new report “Intentional AI: Connecting Intelligence, Capital and Outcomes”, DBS Group Research argues that as AI capabilities become more widely available, access to intelligence alone will become a less durable source of competitive advantage. Instead, organisations will increasingly differentiate themselves through the problems they choose to solve and their ability to translate intelligence into measurable outcomes.
The report suggests that the next phase of the AI economy may be defined less by who can generate the most intelligence and more by who can apply it most effectively to solve real-world challenges. While the first wave of AI focused on capability, the next may increasingly be defined by outcomes.
For Asia, this shift creates a significant opportunity. The report identifies ageing, climate resilience and financial inclusion as some of the region's most consequential challenges and argues that these could also become major drivers of innovation, investment and long-term growth. Key findings include:
1. The next AI advantage may come from solving consequential problems, not building bigger models
DBS Group Research argues that as AI capabilities become more widely diffused, future advantage will increasingly depend on identifying meaningful problems and aligning technology, capital, governance and execution around solving them. The report positions ageing, healthcare access, financial inclusion and climate resilience not only as policy priorities, but as emerging opportunities set for businesses and investors. (Pages 7 – 10, 11 – 14)
While much of the global AI conversation remains focused on foundation models and computing power, Asia accounted for 74% of global industrial robot installations in 2024, compared with 16% for Europe and 9% for the Americas. As AI increasingly moves beyond prediction into action, Asia already possesses significant advantages in deployment, manufacturing and physical systems. (Pages 15 – 16)
AI companies raised approximately USD270 billion in venture funding in 2025, with nearly 80% flowing to North America and 5.7% to Asia. At the same time, Asia faces some of the world’s largest opportunities in ageing, climate resilience and financial inclusion. DBS Group Research argues that as intelligence becomes increasingly abundant, future value creation may depend less on generating intelligence and more on deploying it effectively in sectors where outcomes matter most. (Pages 22 – 28)
Some of Asia's largest opportunities lie in converting intelligence into action. More accurate weather forecasts create value when they improve resilience. Greater access to financial services creates value when it improves financial health and economic agency. Across both domains, durable value comes from connecting intelligence to measurable outcomes. (Pages 17 – 12)
Singapore's comparative advantage lies not in competing on technological scale, but in helping connect Asia's strengths across innovation, manufacturing, deployment, finance, assurance and governance. The report proposes that Singapore can play a distinctive role in making Asian innovation more trusted, interoperable and investable across borders

British Business Bank Backs TSP Ventures with £3m Commitment
summary:
The British Business Bank today announces a £3 million commitment from its Regional Angels Programme, delivered via its partner Haatch, to TSP Ventures – an early-stage venture firm.
TSP Ventures invest in hard science and breakthrough technologies that can deliver sustainable, cost-effective and geo-secure supplies of critical resources like energy, food, water and metals.
Founded in 2019 by founders Chris Smith and Mike Doswell, TSP Ventures has already backed 17 seed stage companies spanning metal recycling, metal-organic frameworks, clean hydrogen, sodium ion batteries and bio-electrochemical waste treatment. These companies have gone onto raise over £125m in follow-on funding and created over 150 jobs in the UK.
This £3 million commitment is from the British Business Bank's Regional Angels Programme, which aims to reduce regional imbalances in access to early-stage equity finance across the UK. The funding will be co-invested alongside capital from TSP's own investor base, supporting founders building high-growth potential businesses across the UK.
Mike Doswell, Co-Founder & Chief Investment Officer of TSP Ventures, said:
We started TSP because we believed that resilient resources – abundant green energy, clean air, plentiful freshwater and food – would define the coming decades, and everything we've seen since has only sharpened that conviction. Having the British Business Bank alongside us is a huge vote of confidence, not just in TSP, but in the founders and teams we're backing
Mark Barry, Senior Investment Director at the British Business Bank, said:
TSP Ventures are investing in businesses across the country which are helping to build the resource resilience of the UK through exciting new technologies in the clean energy industry. We are pleased that this £3 million commitment, through our Regional Angels Programme, will support this continued investment.
Fred Soneya, Co-Founder and General Partner at Haatch, said:
The Regional Angels Programme is designed to increase the supply of early-stage capital across the UK, and delivering it through the Haatch Platform allows experienced investors like TSP Ventures to co-invest alongside the British Business Bank in a simple, scalable way. We’re pleased to support TSP and the founders they back.
